newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business Press - Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business Press - Sept 5.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- REFUGE BOWS TO SHAREHOLDERS

Refuge Group are to adjust the terms of its 1.5 billion pounds stg merger with United Friendly, bowing to institutional shareholder pressure. The group is to create a new security, enabling shareholders access to potential profits from Refuge's 930 million stg ordinary branch funds. The rethink will delay the deal by at least three weeks.
-- LLOYD'S SECURES DTI APPROVAL FOR EQUITAS

Lloyd's of London got the go-ahead for the Equitas reinsurance company it has set up to seal off its huge pre-1993 insurance losses. The government authorisation is the final part of the financial reconstruction of the insurance market to establish its future.
-- TESCO STEPS UP SUPERMARKET PRICE WAR

Tesco unveiled plans to cut the price of more than 600 products from next Monday, investing 30 million stg to pay for the price cuts. Shares in supermarket groups fell sharply after the announcement. Under the offer, Tesco, Britain's biggest supermarket group, is promising that if a customer can find one of the 600 products for less, it will refund twice the difference.
THE TIMES
-- MORGAN SEEKS ASSET FREEZE ON MANAGER

A joint legal action has been taken out by Morgan Grenfell and Royal Bank of Scotland to freeze the assets of Peter Young, manager of the three Morgan Grenfell funds at the centre of an investigation by the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (Imro). Young was suspended from his job on Monday after being interviewed by Imro officials.
-- JOBS AT RISK AS BOOKER BIDS TO CARRY OFF N&P

A proposed takeover of Nurdin & Peacock by Booker, the rival cash and carry and food wholesaling company, could put more than 1,200 jobs at risk. The Nurdin board has recommended the deal which would give Booker 38 per cent of the UK's cash and carry market. Chief executive of Booker, Charles Bowen said that around 40 of the two companies' 213 depots will be shut. -- TRAFALGAR SUED OVER RITZ DEAL The construction and engineering group Trafalgar House is being sued over the sale of the Ritz Hotel in a lawsuit brought by Agincourt Associates who claims that it is owed 750,000 stg for help that it gave Trafalgar in finding a buyer for the Ritz. The little known firm claims that it introduced several potential buyers and was instrumental in the eventual sale to Ellerman Investments.
THE GUARDIAN
-- STRIKE THREAT AT NATWEST

Following a breakdown in pay talks more than 1,000 staff at NatWest Life, the life assurance ARM of the high street bank, are to be balloted for industrial action tomorrow. The dispute stems from proposed changes to the way in which the regulated sales force staff would be paid. NatWest wants to introduce a system in which salaries are linked to sales targets.
-- RESIGNATION OF ALLEVIATE'S CHAIRMAN LIFTS SHARES

The resignation of Alleviate chairman, Carlo De Bennedetti has been seen by investors as a sign that the company would revive after five years of losses. Yesterday morning trading in Alleviate shares was suspended for 45 minutes by Milan bourse authorities after they leaped almost 13 per cent exceeding trading limits. They later fell back and closed at just over 3 per cent up.
-- CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRY BACK IN RECESSION, SURVEYORS WARN

According to the Royal Institute of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), the construction industry is back in recession. Issuing a warning in advance of government construction figures due to be published tomorrow, RICS said that a further 40,000 jobs would be lost this year, despite optimism in the housing market. They blamed the failure of the Government's Private Finance Initiative to replace dwindling publicly funded investment quickly as well as the sluggish response of house builders to the housing market recovery. THE INDEPENDENT
-- UK TO BEAR BRUNT OF LUCAS CUTS

Around 500 jobs are to be lost, after a restructuring programme, at the UK operations of Lucas-Varity, the car parts and aerospace giant, formed two months ago in a 3.2 billion stg merger. Victor Rice the new chief executive as reviewed the management structures which will result in the loss of 50 of the 150 senior administrative jobs. A further 450 administrative jobs will be cut over the next few months. -- P-REG CAR SALES FAIL TO REACH 500,000 MARK

Registration data suggests that around 475,000 new P-registration cars were sold last month, only one per cent up on last year. Manufacturers had predicted a more buoyant August with sales of around 490,000, and had even hoped that sales could surge through the 500,000 barrier for the first time since 1989. The statistics will also show a bad month for Ford and Vauxhall, and a continuing boom in sales of imported cars.
-- CHANNEL 5 TO SEEK CLOSE TIES WITH BSKYB

Channel 5 Broadcasting is to seek close commercial ties with BSkyB in a move that could include joint programme acquisition and cross-promotion as well as an agreement to distribute Channel 5 on satellite. The strategy is aimed at improving channel 5's coverage nation-wide, while BSkyB would use the tie to encourage the take-up of satellite dishes and promote its 40 pay-television channels.
